# Rendering, and keeping it fast {#sec-rendering}

## Two buttons, two commands

**Render** builds the whole project into `_book/` (or `docs/`). In RStudio it
is the toolbar button; from a terminal it is `quarto render`.

**Preview** starts a live server that re-renders on save and refreshes the
browser. In RStudio this is what *Render on Save* gives you; from a terminal it
is `quarto preview`.

You can work entirely from the buttons for an ordinary book. Two exceptions
where you need `quarto preview` in the Terminal instead:

- **Anything that needs a real web server** — live webR cells (@sec-webr) are
  dead over a `file://` address.
- **Any custom format**, `live-html` included. RStudio only auto-previews
  formats it knows, so Render prints *"Output created"* and no window appears.

`quarto preview` builds, serves at `http://localhost:####`, opens a browser,
and re-renders on save. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> stops it.

## `freeze` and `cache`

Both stop Quarto re-running code unnecessarily. They solve **different**
problems and live in different places, and the distinction is worth teaching
clearly because the names do not help.

::: {.callout-note}
## `freeze` — file level, about *portability*
With `freeze: auto`, Quarto runs a chapter's code once, stores the results in a
`_freeze/` folder, and reuses them until that `.qmd` changes.

Commit `_freeze/` to Git and the payoff is large: a colleague — or a build
server — can render the whole book **without** having R and every package
installed, because the computed results travel with the repository.

`freeze: true` never re-runs. `freeze: false` always runs fresh.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## `cache` — chunk level, about *speed while writing*
`cache: true` uses knitr's cache to skip re-running an individual chunk whose
code has not changed, so a slow simulation does not re-run on every preview.
The caches live in per-chapter `*_cache/` folders.
:::

**Rule of thumb:** `cache` for "this chunk is slow while I am writing",
`freeze` for "someone else should be able to build this without my setup".
They combine, and both can be overridden per file or per chunk.

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
  cache: false
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Cached results can go stale
Both mechanisms trust the source text, not the world. If a chunk reads a data
file and the *file* changes but the *code* does not, you will keep the old
result. Delete `_freeze/` and `*_cache/` and re-render when you have changed
anything a chunk depends on but does not contain.
:::

## What actually makes a book slow

In practice, in this order:

1. **Code that runs on every render.** Fix with `freeze: auto`.
2. **A LaTeX PDF build.** Fix by only rendering the PDF when you need it:
   Render → *Render Book* → HTML only, or `quarto render --to html`.
3. **Huge images.** See @sec-figures — keep them under about 500 kB.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Render one chapter while drafting
`quarto preview 08-iframes.qmd` renders just that file. In RStudio, pressing
Render while a single `.qmd` is open does the same thing. Cross-references to
other chapters will not resolve in that preview — that is expected, and they
come back in a full render.
:::
